u0091: Propensity and NBA/NBO. Propensity models by product category, first at Carrefour and today at Smiles. I created the NBA (Next Best Action), which decides which action to take with each customer. The next step is the NBO (Next Best Offer), which also chooses which offer to deliver.
u0092: Causal inference. Propensity tells you who tends to buy, not who buys because of the campaign. That's why I use control groups and holdouts to measure incrementality.

u0095: Generative AI. Multi-agent systems with LangGraph and MCP, conversational chats to extract insights from data, such as SmilesGPT, and applications that support agile development of digital solutions.

u0105: Governance of control groups. Measuring incrementality is a statistical problem: the control group must stay untouched and comparable to the treated group. But it is only solved through a management decision: who owns the control group, who may contact it and for how long. I proposed that the D&A team take over this management for the propensity models at Smiles, a condition for evolving from NBA to NBO with gains that can be proven.

u0110: DataBank and the Gutenberg algorithm: propensity, CRM activation and incrementality measured with a control group.
u0112: Historical purchase data became incremental revenue, with the gain proven against a control group: R$ 45 million in under 60 days.
u0114: Every retailer keeps years of purchase history, but usually treats it as a by-product of operations. DataBank, which I co-founded, started from the opposite idea: treat that history as an asset and build on it a product able to generate revenue and to prove that this revenue is new. In 2022 the startup was recognized at the Innovation Challenge of Tech for Retail, in Paris.
u0119: Purchase dataCustomers' purchase history as the raw material.
u0120: Propensity modelGutenberg estimates who is most likely to buy each product or category.
u0121: SegmentationAudiences ranked by propensity, ready for the advertiser or for CRM.
u0122: ActivationCampaigns on owned CRM channels, with Media Trading and CRM in the same flow.
u0123: MeasurementResults compared with a control group that was not contacted.
u0125: Only what exceeds what the control group, with no contact, would have bought anyway counts as platform revenue. That is what separates data monetization from inflated attribution.
u0128: The model learns from what customers actually bought, without depending on third-party data. The quality of the ranking comes from the depth of the history.
u0130: Whoever controls the channel controls who is contacted, when and with which message. That makes the campaign measurable end to end.
u0131: A control group that is not contacted
u0132: Keeping some customers untouched lets you read the difference in results as the effect of the campaign, and not as a purchase that would have happened anyway.
u0135: A new revenue line from an asset that already exists: customers' own purchase data.
u0136: For the industry and the advertiser
u0137: Media that reaches the people most likely to buy, with results measured against a control group.
u0139: More relevant offers on the channels they already use, instead of mass communication.
u0140: Recognition in Paris. u0306: Preço Feito: the lowest price each item can have without a loss.
u0309: The price that pays the bills. Send your purchase invoices and the menu: Preço Feito shows the lowest price each item can have without a loss, with the math open. All from your phone.
u0311: Many people who sell food set prices by looking at the neighbor or by gut feeling. Few know what the dish leaving the kitchen really costs: ingredient costs change with every invoice, the monthly bills (rent, electricity, water, gas, internet, staff) must be spread across what is sold, and spreadsheets are a chore and age fast. The result is selling below what you should without noticing.
u0313: Send the purchase invoices (XML, PDF or a photo of the receipt). Preço Feito separates each ingredient and calculates the cost per kilo, liter or unit. Without an invoice, you can type the value by hand.
u0315: Send the menu or product list as a PDF or photo. The AI suggests which ingredients from your stock each item uses, and builds the recipe sheet for you to just review.
u0317: Enter the business bills. The AI splits the month's cost across what you sell, accounting for prep losses, packaging and fees.
u0319: See the minimum price of each item, the one that pays the bills without a loss. Tap any number and see the whole calculation, from the cost of the bun to the rent.
u0321: No spreadsheet. You send what you already have (invoices and menu) and the product organizes the rest.
u0322: The AI does the boring part. It builds the sheet for each item and spreads the monthly bills. You just review.
u0323: Every number explained. No black box: the price recalculates on the spot when you change a cost.
u0324: Made for people with no time, designed for the phone, at the pace of a bar or restaurant's day to day.
u0327: Dishes, portions and drinks with a recipe sheet: every ingredient on the invoice goes into the dish cost.
u0329: Snacks, pastries and recipes that yield several units, with prep loss and packaging in the calculation.
u0331: Grocers, neighborhood markets, delis and produce stores: direct cost from the invoice plus a share of the store's bills.
u0333: The name plays on “prato feito”, the PF: a settled, honest, everyday price, in the language of people who work in the sector. The symbol is a plate seen from above with cutlery and a check in the center, with the lime highlighter-marker accent. The voice is clear and direct, without jargon, as in “The X-Salada needs at least R$ 22.40 to pay for itself”.

u0360: They want to refresh the menu and check whether current prices still make sense.
